what_it_does: Autonomous vehicles must run perception systems (computer vision and lidar processing) to understand their surroundings, but running these full systems continuously wastes compute power on irrelevant scenes. AnA (an Attentive Autonomous Driving system) mimics human attention: the planning module expresses what it needs to know (e.g., 'detect pedestrians nearby') and the perception system responds with only those focused calculations rather than running all perception tasks uniformly. The system distinguishes between background awareness (always-on but low-resolution sensing) and focused attention (high-precision sensing on safety-critical elements like nearby pedestrians), switching modes dynamically based on what the planner needs to make safe decisions.
